persons.name: Cakrarāja
persons.evidence: vibudhaś cakrarājaḥ sudhīraḥ śukle pakṣe vividharacanaṃ lekhayāmāsa

date.as_written: kāle dyocāraṇavikalite, śuddhanepālaśāke, māghe māse śaśadharadine ... śrīpañcamyāṃ ... śukle pakṣe

notes: Year is given in a chronogram-like phrase (dyocāraṇavikalite) that I did not decode. The year 906 comes from the catalogue, and "śuddhanepālaśāke" fits NS. The verse is ambiguous: "vibudhaś cakrarājaḥ ... lekhayāmāsa kena" could mean Cakrarāja had the copy made (commissioner) or wrote it himself. I follow the catalogue and list him as scribe. No king, donor or other person is named.
